source: The analytics endpoint returns daily counts for a requested project and date range. Dates use the project's configured time zone, which can differ from the caller's local time zone. The endpoint accepts no more than ninety consecutive days in one request; longer reports require multiple calls. Counts for the current day can change as events arrive, and the service marks that day as provisional. Older days are normally finalized after forty-eight hours, though a documented backfill may revise them later. The response includes the time zone identifier and an updated_at timestamp so clients can show the context beside a chart. A missing day means no events were recorded, not a request failure. The API returns an error object for an invalid project identifier or a range above the limit. Cache responses for at most five minutes if a report includes today; historical reports may use a longer cache.
objective: Write an API documentation section explaining date boundaries, count freshness, and request limits. Include guidance for interpreting missing days.
creator: C

source: The portable lamp has three brightness settings controlled by one button. A short press cycles through low, medium, high, and off. Holding the button for two seconds while the lamp is on starts a thirty-minute timer; the lamp blinks twice to confirm. The timer turns the lamp off but does not change the brightness setting used next time. The lamp can run while plugged in, although charging may take longer at high brightness. Its battery indicator has four segments and estimates remaining charge rather than exact minutes. The test team observed about six hours on medium in a room at 21 degrees Celsius; cold storage and aging batteries may shorten that time. The quick-start card currently says only to charge the lamp before first use. Customer support wants the timer behavior included because callers sometimes mistake the automatic shutoff for a fault. The packaging team has space for roughly one short paragraph and a small numbered list.
objective: Create a quick-start instruction for the lamp that covers the button, timer, charging, and what the battery indicator means.
creator: C

source: The school library's reservation form lets students request a book that is currently checked out. It does not reserve books that are already on the shelf; students can borrow those at the desk. Requests are processed in the order received, but a class set can be held for a scheduled lesson ahead of individual requests. When a copy returns, the first eligible student receives an email and has three school days to collect it. Weekends and holidays do not count toward that window. If the student does not collect it, the library contacts the next person. The form shows a queue position, which may change when damaged copies are removed or class holds are added. Staff cannot promise a return date because borrowers may renew a book when nobody is waiting. A student who needs a title for an imminent assignment can ask a librarian about an alternative edition or another branch.
objective: Write a student FAQ answer explaining reservations, queue position, and pickup timing. Include when to ask a librarian for help.
creator: C

source: A field technician is replacing the filter in a small water sampler. The instrument should be powered down and disconnected from the charging cable before the housing opens. The used filter can retain water, so the technician places an absorbent pad below the housing. The replacement filter has an arrow showing flow direction; installing it backward can reduce the sample volume. After closing the housing, the technician runs a two-minute rinse into a waste container and checks the seam for leaks. A dry seam after the rinse is a useful check, but it does not verify the accuracy of the next sample. The service manual calls for a calibration check if the device was dropped or if flow remains low after a new filter. Most routine swaps need no calibration. Used filters go into the site's designated waste stream, which varies by sampling location and local procedure. The team has asked for instructions a new hire can follow at the bench.
objective: Write a numbered filter replacement procedure. Preserve the safety steps, post-installation check, and condition for calibration.
creator: C

source: The query planner builds an index scan when a filter matches a field with a usable index. It estimates the number of matching rows from stored statistics, then compares the scan cost with a full table read. Those statistics are refreshed nightly for most collections. A newly loaded collection may have stale statistics until the next refresh, so the chosen plan can be slower than expected. Developers can request a plan preview without running the query; the preview shows the chosen path and estimated row count, not the actual runtime. A plan may also change after a schema migration or a large data import. The team recommends checking a slow query with current statistics before adding another index, because each new index adds write cost. This advice applies to routine performance tuning; an incident response may require a faster temporary measure. The planner does not guarantee that an index will be used merely because the filtered field is indexed.
objective: Explain in a developer note why an indexed query might still scan a table. Include how to inspect the plan and when to revisit statistics.
creator: C

source: The meal-planning app now lets households mark an ingredient as already on hand. Marked ingredients disappear from the shopping list for that plan, but they remain visible in the recipe and its quantities. The setting is per household and per plan, so marking rice for this week's plan does not carry into next week's plan. Anyone in the household can change the mark. In a small test, participants said this reduced duplicate purchases, although the team did not measure actual spending. The initial release covers ingredients added by the app's recipes. Ingredients typed as free-form shopping notes will still appear until the user removes them manually. The product team is considering a future pantry inventory feature, but no date or scope has been agreed. The release copy needs to help a household understand the immediate behavior without promising automatic stock tracking. A support article will separately explain how to undo a mark if it was made by mistake.
objective: Write in-app announcement copy for the ingredient marking feature. Explain its scope, effect on the list, and how long the mark lasts.
creator: C

source: The training coordinator interviewed two shift supervisors about a new handoff checklist. One supervisor said the checklist made missing maintenance notes easier to spot during the morning shift. The other liked the consistent order but worried that workers might treat an empty box as proof a task was complete. The checklist has fields for equipment status, unresolved issues, and the next shift's contact. It is currently used on the packaging line during weekday handoffs; weekend crews still use their existing log. During the first month, coordinators reviewed twenty handoffs and found four with an unresolved issue recorded in the checklist. They did not compare that count with the old process. The supervisors agree that urgent equipment problems still require a direct call, even when the issue is written down. The operations manager will decide whether to extend the checklist after a second month of use and feedback from weekend staff. No extension has been approved yet.
objective: Write a short internal interview summary covering the supervisors' views, current use, and next decision point.
creator: C

source: The help center offers downloadable copies of invoices for completed orders. A buyer opens the order history page, selects an order, and chooses Download invoice. The invoice lists the items and tax charged at checkout. It may not reflect a refund issued later; refunds appear in a separate credit note attached to the same order. Draft orders do not have invoices. Business buyers can enter a company name before checkout, but support cannot add a company name to an invoice after an order is complete. For orders placed before the new checkout launched in March, some invoice downloads may be missing; support can provide the original receipt after verifying the order number and email. A customer who needs a tax correction should contact support with the order number, rather than editing the PDF. The team wants this distinction made clear because recent tickets have confused invoices and credit notes.
objective: Write a help-center FAQ about downloading invoices. Cover refunds, missing older invoices, and company details.
creator: C

source: A batch importer reads a UTF-8 CSV with a header row and one product per subsequent row. The required columns are sku, name, and quantity. A blank quantity is an error; zero is a valid quantity that keeps the product listed as out of stock. The importer validates all rows before making changes, then reports line numbers for any errors. If validation fails, no products are updated. For a valid file, existing products with matching SKUs are updated and new SKUs are created. The importer does not delete products absent from the file. A successful import report lists created and updated counts, but processing can take several minutes for files near the 20,000-row limit. The web page can be closed while a job runs; its status remains available in import history. Operators should review the report before sending a catalog announcement because an accepted file can still contain an unintended but syntactically valid price or description.
objective: Draft concise importer documentation covering file format, validation behavior, updates, and how to review a completed job.
creator: C

source: The office building uses occupancy sensors to dim lights in meeting rooms after ten minutes without detected movement. The sensor does not switch off the emergency lighting circuit. People working quietly may need to wave or tap the wall control to restore full brightness; the facilities team has received three reports of this in the north wing. The control by the door also allows a manual dim level during a meeting. At the end of a booking, the room controller returns to automatic mode. Facilities plans to adjust sensor sensitivity in two rooms next month if a short trial shows fewer unwanted dimming events without leaving lights bright in empty rooms. No building-wide change has been scheduled. Staff should report a room that stays dark after using the wall control, since that may indicate a separate electrical fault. The system's energy estimate comes from expected lamp hours and has not been verified against a meter.
objective: Write a staff notice explaining normal dimming behavior, the manual control, and when to report a problem.
creator: C

source: The archive search service stores a text index of public meeting minutes. A new document enters the index after a processing job extracts its text and metadata. Scanned pages with poor contrast may produce incomplete text, so a search result is not proof that every page contains the exact displayed phrase. Users can open the original PDF to confirm wording. Documents are usually searchable within one working day of publication, but the archive team pauses indexing during occasional metadata corrections. Search filters include meeting date and committee; the date filter refers to the meeting date, not the day the PDF was uploaded. Removed or replaced minutes can leave an old search result visible until the next index refresh, which runs every six hours. The archive staff plan to add a visible processing status next season. Until then, the site shows the PDF directly as soon as it is published even if its text is not yet searchable.
objective: Explain how archive search works for a public help page. Include indexing delay, scanned documents, and the meaning of the date filter.
creator: C

source: The bike-share operator is trialing a return confirmation screen at twelve stations. After a rider docks a bike, the screen shows whether the dock has registered the return. A green confirmation usually appears within five seconds when the station is online. If no confirmation appears, the rider should check that the bike is locked and use the app's trip screen or call the number on the dock. The display is informational; the trip record in the operator's system determines billing. At two trial stations with unstable connections, confirmations have appeared late even though returns were recorded on time. The operator has not found evidence that those delays changed charges, but is still reviewing logs. Riders at stations outside the trial will continue to see the older indicator light. The team will decide whether to expand the screen after collecting six weeks of rider feedback and connection data. The trial began this Monday.
objective: Write a rider FAQ answer explaining the new return screen and what to do when confirmation is missing. State where it is available.
creator: C

source: The design interview focused on a reading app's adjustable line spacing. The designer said early testers asked for more room between lines on long articles, especially when reading on a phone during a commute. The current control offers three spacing choices in the reader settings, and the choice stays with the account across devices. It does not change the layout of downloaded PDF files, which retain their original page design. In a test with eighteen volunteers, eleven selected the widest spacing at least once; the study did not establish which choice improved comprehension. The designer wants to add a live preview beside the control, but that idea remains a prototype. Engineering has committed to fixing a separate issue where spacing resets on older Android builds. The designer also cautioned that the widest setting can make footnotes harder to keep near their references in narrow windows. The next usability round will include people using screen magnification.
objective: Turn these interview notes into a short product story about line spacing. Include current behavior, its limits, and the planned next steps.
creator: C

source: A community garden uses a shared calendar for watering shifts. Volunteers sign up for a morning or evening slot and mark it complete after watering. If rain has soaked the beds, the volunteer may skip watering but should record Rain in the shift note so the next person understands the gap. The coordinator checks the soil each Sunday and may change the schedule during a heat wave. The posted schedule is therefore a starting plan, not an instruction to water regardless of conditions. New volunteers should use the marked watering cans because their capacity matches the posted amounts. Most raised beds take one can; seedlings in the south beds take only half a can unless the coordinator posts a different amount. Volunteers should avoid watering leaves in strong afternoon sun and report a broken hose in the calendar note. The garden asks for a concise guide that can be printed near the tool shed.
objective: Write a brief volunteer watering guide with sign-up, completion, weather exceptions, and bed amounts.
creator: C

source: The mobile app caches recent transit departures so the station screen opens quickly. When a connection is available, it requests fresh times and shows the update time beneath the list. If the request fails, the app keeps the last cached list for up to fifteen minutes and labels it as older information. After fifteen minutes it replaces the times with a message directing riders to station signs. The cache is per station and route; switching routes does not make the old route's times appear as current. Live departure estimates come from the transit provider and can change without notice as vehicles move. The app team has seen occasional differences of two or three minutes between the app and platform signs, but has not isolated a single cause. Scheduled times are shown when the provider sends no live estimate, and those entries carry a schedule label. The screen does not promise a train will arrive at the displayed minute.
objective: Write a clear explanation for riders of departure-time freshness, fallback behavior, and schedule labels.
creator: C

source: The photo desk accepts image submissions through a form with fields for the photographer, location, date, and a short caption. Staff review each submission before it appears in the community gallery. The review checks that the image is relevant and that the submitter has permission to share it; approval is not automatic. Images showing identifiable children require a guardian's written permission, even when the event was public. A submitter can ask to remove an image after publication by contacting the desk with the submission number. The desk aims to review submissions within five working days, but festival weeks can take longer. Accepted images may be cropped for the gallery thumbnail while the full image remains available on its detail page. The desk does not accept watermarked promotional graphics through this form. Staff have asked for instructions that keep the requirements visible without making the process seem more complicated than it is.
objective: Write submission instructions for the community photo gallery. Include review timing, permission requirements, and removal requests.
creator: C

source: The service desk received fourteen calls about the new appointment page during its first two days. Nine callers could not find the reschedule link, which appears below the confirmation details on a phone screen. Three callers were trying to change appointments made at a partner clinic; those bookings are handled on the clinic's site. The remaining two reported that the page stopped responding after they tapped Save, but we have not reproduced that problem. Support can send a direct link for our own appointments while the layout team reviews placement. We should avoid telling all callers to use that link, because it will not open partner bookings. I suggest a small copy change this week and a follow-up check after another week of call logs.
objective: Could you turn this into a short reply our support agents can use? Explain where the reschedule link sits and why partner-clinic bookings need a different route, then include the URL agents should send for our appointments. Please keep the Save issue as unconfirmed while we investigate it.
creator: D

source: The first batch of repaired laptops is ready for pickup. We received twelve devices from the community center; eight now start reliably, two still need replacement batteries, and two have screen damage beyond our volunteer team's current tools. The eight working devices have passed a basic charging and keyboard check, but they have not been tested with every accessibility setting the center uses. We can deliver them on Friday if the center confirms that someone can sign for them. I have asked the repair lead to price the batteries before we commit to a second batch. We should thank the volunteers for their time while being precise about what is complete. Several families are waiting, so an accurate handoff date matters more than an optimistic one.
objective: Please make this a handoff update for the community center: separate the eight ready laptops from the four still needing work, mention the limited testing, and thank the volunteers. Add the Friday pickup time once it's confirmed, and keep delivery conditional on someone being available to sign.
creator: D

source: The volunteer orientation is booked for Wednesday evening in the small meeting room. Eleven people registered, although past sessions usually lose one or two attendees on the day. We have printed ten handbooks and can make more at the library if everyone comes. The session should run for about an hour, followed by optional time for questions. A trainer suggested adding a short demonstration of the sign-in tablet because two volunteers struggled with it last month. I agree, provided we do not cut the section on safeguarding records. The tablet demonstration is practice, not a requirement for people who will work only on the phone line. Please leave enough time for the trainer to explain where volunteers can ask for help later.
objective: Could you draft a reminder email for Wednesday's orientation that covers the hour-long session, optional questions, and a brief tablet practice without crowding out safeguarding? Include the meeting room's building address so new volunteers know where to go, and make clear the tablet is optional for phone-line volunteers.
creator: D

source: On my first day at the new studio, I put my notebooks in a drawer and kept looking for them in the old place. The room faces a busy street, so the quiet I had imagined is rare before lunch. By midafternoon the light reaches the back wall, and that has become my favorite time to sketch. I finished three small studies this week, but none feels ready to show. A friend asked whether the move has made me more productive. I do not know yet; packing and setting up took most of the month, and I am still learning what hours suit the room. What has changed is that I now have a place where I can leave a drawing unfinished and come back to it.
objective: I want this reflection to say how long I've rented the new studio. Can you work that detail into the passage without making the move sound like an instant productivity boost?
creator: D

source: Our team tested the revised sign-up form with six returning members on Monday. Five completed it without help; one stopped at the emergency contact field because the form did not say whether that contact was required. The field is optional under our policy, but the interface currently marks it with the same styling as required fields. The design lead proposed adding an explicit optional label and a short explanation of why we ask. Engineering estimates that change at half a day, assuming no validation changes are needed. We have not tested the form with first-time members yet, so the six sessions cannot tell us how new visitors will fare. I suggest making the label change, then scheduling a separate first-time member check before the wider launch.
objective: Please tighten this update around the optional emergency-contact label and the need to test first-time members before launch. Add the scheduled date for that follow-up check if we have one; don't present the six returning-member sessions as evidence about new visitors.
creator: D

source: The garden club has offered to host our repair cafe in its hall on the first Saturday of each month. The hall is free, but we would need to bring extension leads and arrange a volunteer to unlock the building. Our current quarterly sessions average twenty-five visitors, and no one has measured demand for a monthly schedule. Two experienced repairers can attend in October; neither has committed for later dates. The club would like an answer by September 18 so it can publish its calendar. I recommend accepting one trial date in October and reviewing attendance and volunteer availability afterward. If we do that, the public announcement should call it a trial session rather than a standing monthly service. The arrangement could be useful, but it needs a manageable start.
objective: Could you shape this into a reply to the garden club proposing the October trial, with the practical needs and the September 18 decision deadline clear? Include the October Saturday date they offered, and avoid promising a monthly program before we've checked demand and volunteer availability.
creator: D

source: The municipal records office receives requests for copies through its portal, by mail, and at the front counter. Portal submissions receive an automatic receipt number, but that number confirms delivery rather than completeness. Staff review each request for a usable description of the record and an address for response. If the description is too broad, a specialist contacts the requester for clarification before searching; the office does not treat that contact as a denial. Routine requests are usually fulfilled within ten business days of a complete submission, although archived files may take longer to retrieve. Certified copies require a fee and must be mailed or collected in person because the seal cannot be delivered as an ordinary download. Staff may waive copy charges for requests under five pages when the cost of collection would exceed the fee. The office publishes weekly queue updates, but those estimates do not change any statutory deadlines.
objective: For the public procedure, please state the exact statutory deadline that applies to a completed records request, while keeping the distinction between that deadline and the office's usual ten-business-day turnaround.
creator: D

source: Researchers surveyed 184 graduate students at one public university about their use of shared laboratory equipment. Most respondents reported checking the online reservation calendar before arriving, while fewer than half said they routinely recorded maintenance concerns in the log. The survey was voluntary and conducted during a semester when two major instruments were out of service, which may have affected responses. Students who reported prior equipment training were more likely to report using the log, but the survey cannot show that training caused the behavior. Interview comments suggested that some students viewed the log as a place for urgent faults only. The authors propose testing a clearer log prompt next term and comparing entries before and after its introduction. They do not claim the prompt will improve equipment uptime. The study's main contribution is a description of how students say they use the current system at this site.
objective: Could you add the survey's response rate to this methods summary so readers can judge how much of the graduate-student population took part?
creator: D

source: At the regional transit accessibility meeting, riders described inconsistent audio announcements on two older bus routes. The fleet supervisor said replacement speakers are on order for twelve vehicles, but delivery has not been confirmed. Operations will test three vehicles that already received repairs during the next two weeks. If those tests show reliable volume at the rear seats, maintenance will use the same setup for the remaining repaired vehicles; a poor result would prompt a new equipment review. A rider representative asked for a public timetable, and the chair agreed to publish a progress note after the tests. The meeting did not approve a date for full fleet completion. Staff also noted that portable stop signs remain available during planned detours, although drivers may need to request them from dispatch. The secretary recorded the rider group's concern that an equipment fix alone may not solve missed announcements when route data is entered incorrectly.
objective: Please turn these notes into a concise update for riders: describe the three-vehicle test, the conditional next step, and the planned progress note. Add the date the replacement speakers are due to arrive if procurement has provided one; keep the full-fleet completion date open.
creator: D

source: A university committee compared three approaches to reducing water use in teaching laboratories. Faucet aerators had the lowest estimated installation cost, while recirculating chillers offered the largest projected savings in the two buildings with high cooling demand. The estimates came from utility records covering twelve months, and the authors caution that unusually warm weather may have raised that year's cooling use. One department has already purchased chillers for its own equipment; the committee has not approved a campus-wide purchase. The report recommends installing aerators in laboratories scheduled for renovation and commissioning a more detailed chiller assessment before requesting capital funds. It also suggests adding water-use orientation to student training, but no estimate of savings from training is available. The committee expects a facilities update next spring. Any comparison of the options should retain the distinction between measured historic use and projected savings under the proposed equipment changes.
objective: Please add the estimated water savings in liters for the proposed aerators to this comparison, while preserving the difference between recorded utility use and projected equipment savings.
creator: D

source: The school district reviewed attendance at its after-school reading program across six elementary sites. Average weekly attendance rose from 71 to 84 students between the first and second terms. The increase coincided with a new bus route at two sites, but coordinators did not collect enough information to attribute the change to transport. One site lost sessions for two weeks during building repairs; its term averages should therefore be interpreted cautiously. Teachers said that shorter reading groups appeared easier to staff, while families asked for more consistent pickup times. The district will keep the current program at all six sites through June and ask principals to submit staffing and transport notes each month. A proposal to add a seventh site is under review for the following year, subject to space and budget. The board has not voted on that expansion. Staff will share the attendance summary with families after verifying the site-level counts.
objective: Could you revise this for families so the attendance change and the plan through June are easy to follow, with the seventh site clearly still under review? Include the date when the verified site-level summary will be shared, if staff have set it, and avoid crediting the new bus route for the increase.
creator: D

source: During a joint planning session, the hospital discharge team and two community agencies discussed weekend referrals for home support. The agencies said they can receive electronic referrals on Saturdays, but acceptance depends on available staff and a verified service address. The discharge team proposed sending referrals by noon Friday when a weekend discharge is anticipated; clinicians noted that discharge timing often changes after that point. Participants agreed to test a revised referral form on one ward for four weeks, beginning next month. They did not agree to a hospital-wide launch. The form will include a field for an alternate contact because agencies sometimes cannot reach a patient immediately after discharge. The ward manager will collect cases in which a referral needs correction and report them at the next joint meeting. Agency representatives also requested that the hospital distinguish an estimated discharge date from a confirmed one in every transmission.
objective: Please specify which ward will run the four-week referral-form trial so the agencies know where to direct questions about corrections.
creator: D

source: The analytics endpoint returns daily counts for a requested project and date range. Dates use the project's configured time zone, which can differ from the caller's local time zone. The endpoint accepts no more than ninety consecutive days in one request; longer reports require multiple calls. Counts for the current day can change as events arrive, and the service marks that day as provisional. Older days are normally finalized after forty-eight hours, though a documented backfill may revise them later. The response includes the time zone identifier and an updated_at timestamp so clients can show the context beside a chart. A missing day means no events were recorded, not a request failure. The API returns an error object for an invalid project identifier or a range above the limit. Cache responses for at most five minutes if a report includes today; historical reports may use a longer cache.
objective: Could you make this API guidance easier for a client developer to scan, especially the project time zone, provisional current-day counts, and the ninety-day limit? Add the endpoint's request-rate limit if one has been set, and retain the advice about shorter caching when today is included.
creator: D

source: The school library's reservation form lets students request a book that is currently checked out. It does not reserve books that are already on the shelf; students can borrow those at the desk. Requests are processed in the order received, but a class set can be held for a scheduled lesson ahead of individual requests. When a copy returns, the first eligible student receives an email and has three school days to collect it. Weekends and holidays do not count toward that window. If the student does not collect it, the library contacts the next person. The form shows a queue position, which may change when damaged copies are removed or class holds are added. Staff cannot promise a return date because borrowers may renew a book when nobody is waiting. A student who needs a title for an imminent assignment can ask a librarian about an alternative edition or another branch.
objective: Please add the email address students should use to ask a librarian about another edition or branch when an assignment deadline is close.
creator: D

source: The query planner builds an index scan when a filter matches a field with a usable index. It estimates the number of matching rows from stored statistics, then compares the scan cost with a full table read. Those statistics are refreshed nightly for most collections. A newly loaded collection may have stale statistics until the next refresh, so the chosen plan can be slower than expected. Developers can request a plan preview without running the query; the preview shows the chosen path and estimated row count, not the actual runtime. A plan may also change after a schema migration or a large data import. The team recommends checking a slow query with current statistics before adding another index, because each new index adds write cost. This advice applies to routine performance tuning; an incident response may require a faster temporary measure. The planner does not guarantee that an index will be used merely because the filtered field is indexed.
objective: Could you include the command or API call a developer uses to request a plan preview, so this explanation leads naturally into a troubleshooting guide?
creator: D

source: The training coordinator interviewed two shift supervisors about a new handoff checklist. One supervisor said the checklist made missing maintenance notes easier to spot during the morning shift. The other liked the consistent order but worried that workers might treat an empty box as proof a task was complete. The checklist has fields for equipment status, unresolved issues, and the next shift's contact. It is currently used on the packaging line during weekday handoffs; weekend crews still use their existing log. During the first month, coordinators reviewed twenty handoffs and found four with an unresolved issue recorded in the checklist. They did not compare that count with the old process. The supervisors agree that urgent equipment problems still require a direct call, even when the issue is written down. The operations manager will decide whether to extend the checklist after a second month of use and feedback from weekend staff. No extension has been approved yet.
objective: Please add the date when the operations manager will make the extension decision, while keeping the weekday-only use and the need for weekend staff feedback clear.
creator: D

source: A batch importer reads a UTF-8 CSV with a header row and one product per subsequent row. The required columns are sku, name, and quantity. A blank quantity is an error; zero is a valid quantity that keeps the product listed as out of stock. The importer validates all rows before making changes, then reports line numbers for any errors. If validation fails, no products are updated. For a valid file, existing products with matching SKUs are updated and new SKUs are created. The importer does not delete products absent from the file. A successful import report lists created and updated counts, but processing can take several minutes for files near the 20,000-row limit. The web page can be closed while a job runs; its status remains available in import history. Operators should review the report before sending a catalog announcement because an accepted file can still contain an unintended but syntactically valid price or description.
objective: Could you reorganize this import documentation into preparation, validation, and follow-up steps, making the all-or-nothing validation and zero-quantity behavior explicit? Include the maximum CSV file size in megabytes if there is a published limit, and keep the reminder to review accepted content before announcing a catalog update.
creator: D

source: The archive search service stores a text index of public meeting minutes. A new document enters the index after a processing job extracts its text and metadata. Scanned pages with poor contrast may produce incomplete text, so a search result is not proof that every page contains the exact displayed phrase. Users can open the original PDF to confirm wording. Documents are usually searchable within one working day of publication, but the archive team pauses indexing during occasional metadata corrections. Search filters include meeting date and committee; the date filter refers to the meeting date, not the day the PDF was uploaded. Removed or replaced minutes can leave an old search result visible until the next index refresh, which runs every six hours. The archive staff plan to add a visible processing status next season. Until then, the site shows the PDF directly as soon as it is published even if its text is not yet searchable.
objective: Please state where users can report a missing or stale search result while the visible processing status is still being developed.
creator: D
